title: Age-class taxonomy SSOT (T2) is a canonical definition plus two hand-copies; the extractor copy has no excuse
detail: forest-age.ts says the proxy and the pipeline extractors 'cannot import from src/' so they keep local copies. That is true for the Deno proxy but false for extractors.ts, which already imports lookupCompany from ../../src/data/companies (line 13, added by the COMPANY_MAP relay 039738f). extractors.classify() still hardcodes 250/80 and its own ForestClass type. Same for scripts/audit-spatial.ts:124,133 (80/250 literals) and registry.ts:353 cqlFilter 'PROJ_AGE_1 >= 250'. The proxy-consistency audit (Check 9) regex-pins the proxy and extractor thresholds, so drift is caught, but the consolidation left 5 encodings of the two numbers (SSOT, proxy, extractors, audit-spatial, registry CQL) where 2 could be 1 today. Fix: extractors.classify delegates to classifyForestAge(typeof age==='number'?age:null, hd!=null&&String(hd)!=='null'&&String(hd)!==''); audit-spatial imports AGE_THRESHOLDS; registry CQL uses a template literal. Update Check 9's extractor test to assert the import (like Check 10's) instead of regexing thresholds.
bucket_reason: pure delegation to an identical function; the string-'null' guard is preserved at the call site

title: wfs-client finally-block deletes per-layer bookkeeping by key without identity check: duplicate fetches and a stale response can win
detail: Sequence: fetch #1 in flight for layer L (its timer handle T1 is still in debounceTimers because deletion only happens in finally). Call #2 arrives: clearTimeout(T1) no-op, rejectPendingForLayer aborts C1, then sets T2. Fetch #1 rejects with AbortError and its finally runs debounceTimers.delete(L) -- removing T2's handle -- and controllers.delete(L). Call #3 within the debounce window now finds no existing timer, so T2 and T3 both fire: two upstream requests for the same layer. When T3 fires it sets C3, but fetch #2's finally (aborted by T3) then runs controllers.delete(L) and removes C3, so call #4 cannot abort fetch #3; #3 and #4 both resolve and DataLayer.tsx:1216-1217 setData()s whichever lands last -- a superseded viewport's features can overwrite the current one. Separately, rejectPendingForLayer (line 35) never rejects: it deletes the pending entry and attaches a no-op catch, so the debounced-away promise never settles; the awaiting DataLayer call at :1216 hangs forever (its finally never runs -- benign only because a later call's finally repairs loading state). Fix: guard each delete with identity (if (debounceTimers.get(layerId)===timer) ...; if (controllers.get(layerId)===controller) ...), and have rejectPendingForLayer actually reject with a DataFetchError('abort') so callers settle. fetchLayerData still has zero unit tests (08-05 COV-1 unaddressed; the only reference is a never-resolving mock in src/test/pipeline/wfs-layers-d10.test.ts:58).
bucket_reason: demonstrable stale-response race on rapid pans; fix must ship with the missing unit tests

title: DataFetchError (T3) unified the class, not the semantics: three clients, three contracts
detail: forest-carbon-client: 20s timeout, caller AbortSignal composed, 429 -> kind 'rate-limit' with Retry-After, network -> 'network', body-parse -> 'http', caller abort rethrows the raw DOMException. watershed-client: no timeout, no abort, 429 collapses into 'http' (Retry-After lost). wfs-client: no timeout, network failure escapes as a raw TypeError (not a DataFetchError at all), abort escapes as a raw DOMException, 429 collapses into 'http' with the proxy's message string. Consequently FetchErrorKind 'abort' is never constructed anywhere in src/, and the only consumer that branches on .kind is map/page.tsx:231-232 (carbon path). forest-carbon-client.ts:81 also re-declares the kind union as a literal copy instead of aliasing FetchErrorKind, and both deprecated re-exports (ForestCarbonFetchError, WatershedFetchError) are still imported by page.tsx:42. The shared class is real; the shared behaviour is not. Either fold a small fetchJson(url,{signal,timeoutMs}) helper into fetch-errors.ts that all three call, or document that only the carbon path has the full contract.
bucket_reason: changes what wfs-client/watershed-client throw; DataLayer and useWatershedSelection catch paths must be re-verified

Delete the parameter and the NetlifyContext interface (lines 17-22) and the last lint warning in this file goes away without an argsIgnorePattern rule. eslint.config has no argsIgnorePattern configured, so the alternative in the 08-05 'What to watch' note was never applied either.

title: The 2000 ha cutblock exclusion is encoded twice (registry MapLibre filter, proxy CQL) and the consistency audit is blind to the proxy side
evidence: src/lib/layers/registry.ts:228-233 style.filter '< 2000' vs netlify/edge-functions/wfs-proxy.ts:97 cqlFilter 'PLANNED_GROSS_BLOCK_AREA < 2000'; proxy-consistency-audit.test.ts:250-275 only iterates registry layers that define source.cqlFilter
detail: The registry cutblocks entry has no source.cqlFilter, so Check 8's 'CQL filters match' loop never visits it; the proxy filter for cutblocks (and fish-streams' STREAM_ORDER >= 3, which the registry does define) is guarded only in the direction registry->proxy. If someone changes the registry filter to 1500 the proxy keeps serving <2000 and nothing goes red. For cutblocks the WFS path is dormant at runtime (tileSource present, loadData short-circuits), so the live consequence is confined to direct /api/wfs consumers and the e2e live-health probe -- but scented-track.ts:7-11 already documents this number as a public-figure hazard for Phase B. Fix: make the audit bidirectional (fail on proxy cqlFilter with no registry counterpart, or require an explicit sanctioned list), and lift 2000 into one named constant the registry filter, a registry source.cqlFilter, and the proxy mirror all reference.
bucket_reason: audit strengthening plus a constant; no runtime path changes

title: zoom-handoff-audit re-implements DataLayer's tier math so the gap check cannot fail, and the mirror ignores tileSource.minZoom
evidence: src/test/audit/zoom-handoff-audit.test.ts:44-56 (pmtilesMin = rasterMax+1, wfsMin = tileMax+1), 82-97 findGaps, 149-172 per-layer loop; vs src/components/map/DataLayer.tsx:265 (minzoom = tileMinZoom ?? 0)
detail: Because each tier's minZoom is defined as the previous tier's maxZoom+1, findGaps() returns [] for every possible registry value -- the per-layer 'no zoom gaps' test (18 cases) is green by construction. The 08-05 rewrite replaced the vacuous assertion but kept the vacuous model. Worse, the model omits tileSource.minZoom, the crash-gate DataLayer actually passes to MapLibre (logging-risk z9, forest-age z4), so the test would also not notice a gated layer whose zoomRange starts below its gate. Only two assertions read independent registry fields (forest-age rasterOverview.maxZoom <= tileSource.maxZoom, wfsMin <= zoomRange[1]). Fix: compute coverage from the real fields (raster [min,max], pmtiles [tileSource.minZoom ?? raster.max+1, tileSource.maxZoom], wfs [tileMax+1, zoomRange[1]]) and assert every integer zoom in zoomRange is covered by some tier; break a registry value and watch it go red before merging (per the 08-09 revert-proven rule).

title: Proxy fetchWithRetry retries deterministic failures and can spend 93 s on a request no client waits more than 20 s for
evidence: netlify/edge-functions/wfs-proxy.ts:425-471 (MAX_RETRIES=3, FETCH_TIMEOUT=30_000, backoff 1s+2s, catch-all retry incl. HTTP 4xx and WFS ExceptionReport); src/lib/data/forest-carbon-client.ts:69-74 (client budget 20 s)
detail: Every throw inside the loop is retried: an upstream 400 (bad CQL), a 404, and a GeoServer ExceptionReport are all deterministic, yet each costs two more upstream hits plus 3 s of sleep before the 502. Three 30 s timeouts plus backoff is 93 s worst case; the only client with a timeout gives up at 20 s, the browser's default fetch has none, so a stuck upstream holds the isolate and keeps hammering BC's WFS after the user has moved on. Retry only on network errors, 5xx, and the 'upstream timing out' body; fail fast on 4xx/ExceptionReport; cap total wall-clock at something a client will actually wait for. Not a security issue -- the rate limiter is upstream of this -- but it is the proxy's largest avoidable load on the government endpoint.
bucket_reason: changes proxy failure timing; wants a unit test on the retry predicate (wfs-bbox-url.ts shows the pure-module pattern to follow)

title: Verified clean: alias coverage, R2 URL SSOT, proxy security posture, COMPANY_MAP SSOT
evidence: useLayerState.ts:52-54,74,101 + useMapState popstate path (585dd0b diff) for aliases; grep r2.dev/pub-b5568 across src scripts e2e netlify -> only r2-config.ts and the CSP line in netlify.toml:40 (config, cannot import); wfs-proxy.ts:475-493,604-618,682-700; proxy-consistency-audit Check 10
detail: Aliases: applied on every client input path (URL hash, localStorage, history popstate); presets, hotspots, e2e and the proxy LAYER_CONFIG all use the new ids; the proxy carries no alias, so a stale bundle requesting layer=tap-deferrals gets a 400 -- acceptable given immutable fingerprinted assets. R2: the SSOT holds; the one inline hostname is the CSP header in netlify.toml, which has no import mechanism. Proxy: Origin is only echoed back when it is in the two-entry allowlist and Vary: Origin is set, so the browser cache cannot poison across origins; layer is validated against LAYER_CONFIG, bbox/point are numeric-parsed and clamped, zoom is parseInt with NaN check, and the CQL bbox is built from Math.round()ed numbers, so no injection surface; no user input reaches a response header; the rate-limit key prefers the Netlify-set x-nf-client-connection-ip over spoofable x-forwarded-for. The CORS lock is a browser boundary only -- curl still works -- which is fine for public data and is the documented intent. Per-isolate rate limiting is already in the Parking Lot. COMPANY_MAP: extractors import lookupCompany; proxy copy is guarded bidirectionally; both zero-pad. That consolidation landed as claimed.
bucket_reason: nothing to change; recorded so the next refresh does not re-audit it

summary: The slice is structurally sound and the T2/T3 relays did land, but 'single source of truth' was achieved as one canonical definition plus guarded copies rather than one encoding: the age thresholds still live in five places (only two regex-guarded), the 2000 ha cutblock rule in two (the audit blind to the proxy side), and DataFetchError unified the class while the three clients kept three different timeout/abort/429 contracts with the 'abort' kind never thrown. The single most important item is R2-02: wfs-client's finally block deletes per-layer timer and controller entries by key without checking they belong to it, which lets rapid pans fire duplicate upstream fetches and lets a superseded viewport's response overwrite the current one -- original code, never patched, zero unit tests. Second is the audit suite: proxy-consistency, color, opacity, story-consistency, contrast and the client tests are real, but zoom-handoff cannot fail by construction (tiers derived from each other, tileSource.minZoom ignored), schema-audit Check 12 tests a hand-copy of PRIORITY_KEYS that has already drifted from MapPopup while staying green, no audit touches legendItems colours despite ARCHITECTURE invariant 3, and two smaller tests are tautologies. Verified clean: the layer-id aliases cover every client input path and the proxy mirror uses the renamed ids; R2 URL SSOT holds; the proxy's origin lock, parameter validation and rate-limit keying have no bypass; registry is 18 entries with 7 public exactly as ARCHITECTURE says (README's '17 layers' contradicts the charter's narrowed surface); hardcoded layer ids outside data/registry are three documented cases worth leaving. The _context lint warning is removable -- the 08-05 'Netlify signature requirement' claim was wrong.
